title: Caller inherits callee's I/O side effects — only visible with neighbourhood context
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE PROCESS_BATCH(N, OUT)
C     Reads N records from the inventory file and accumulates a total.
C     The actual file I/O is INSIDE INV_READ -- defined in another
C     translation unit. A reader looking at PROCESS_BATCH alone sees
C     no I/O verb and might conclude this routine is pure. The
C     neighbourhood context tells the extractor that INV_READ does
C     VSAM READ (its own spec is already extracted), so this routine
C     INHERITS that I/O side effect.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER I, N
      REAL    OUT, X
      OUT = 0.0
      DO I = 1, N
         CALL INV_READ(I, X)
         OUT = OUT + X
      END DO
      RETURN
      END
notes:
This entry is the regression test for Phase 7.0's neighbourhood
feature. WITHOUT neighbourhood context (legacy per-routine extract),
the LLM sees CALL INV_READ as just a name and produces an open
question 'what does INV_READ do?' WITH neighbourhood context, the
INV_READ callee comes with its spec summary ('VSAM READ ...') and
the LLM lifts that I/O into PROCESS_BATCH's `side_effects`. The
scorer pattern for SE-CSI-1 requires INV_READ or VSAM/file I/O to
appear in a side_effects claim — passes only when the neighbourhood
is attached AND callee specs already exist.

The trap mirrors a real pattern from the Phase 5.6 PayrollEquivalence
harness: AVERAGE-SALARY had to be analyzed alongside the surrounding
DEPTPAY program for the spec to capture the right contract.
